title: Dev/v0.3.0. Reproducible Optuna optimization and preserved search evidence
body:
## Summary

MELITE v0.3.0 replaces fixed-grid hyperparameter search with a declared Optuna optimization budget while preserving the existing nested evaluation and classifier-selection contract.

## Main changes

- Replaces `GridSearchCV` with Optuna/TPE for tunable classifiers.
- Introduces an internal search-space contract supporting discrete, integer, continuous, and conditional parameters.
- Defines a fixed optimization policy seeded from MELITE's canonical `RANDOM_STATE`.
- Exposes `n_trials` as the public optimization-budget control.
- Persists one row per completed optimization search in `optimization_searches.csv`.
- Persists the effective optimization and evaluation contract in `optimization_provenance.json`.
- Preserves `results.csv` as the operational parameter source used by `melite export`.
- Preserves nested outer-CV classifier evaluation and final export semantics.
- Aligns documentation, package metadata, citation metadata, configuration guidance, and the evaluation-workflow figure with v0.3.0.

## Scientific characterization

The v0.3.0 candidate was characterized against the committed v0.2.5 baseline using the frozen B5 characterization condition.

All predefined scientific acceptance criteria passed:

- SVC F1-macro delta: `+0.01325`
- Random Forest F1-macro delta: `+0.00412`
- XGBoost F1-macro delta: `-0.01679`
- predefined acceptance margin: `-0.05`
- selected classifier: SVC in both versions

The estimated workload decreased from `42,208` to `4,816` estimator fits under this characterization condition (~88.6% reduction). End-to-end wall-clock remained comparable and was descriptive rather than an acceptance gate.

Formal evidence is preserved in:

- `B5_calibration.json`
- `B5_characterization.json`

## Validation

- Full test suite: `406 passed`
- MkDocs strict build: passed
- Ruff check: passed
- Ruff format check: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

## Scope

MELITE v0.3.0 retains the fixed supported classifier set:

- SVC
- Random Forest
- XGBoost
- opt-in Stacking

Public registration of custom classifiers remains outside the v0.3.0 scope.

title: Dev/v0.2.4. MELITE v0.2.4 — reproducible classifier evaluation and public API stabilization
body:
## Summary

This PR prepares MELITE v0.2.4 and consolidates the project as a
**Multi-Model Classifier Evaluator** for reproducible model selection on
numeric tabular data.

The release strengthens the evaluation contract, preserves raw outer-CV
evidence, stabilizes the public API and packaged example workflow, and adds
permanent static-analysis and formatting gates.

## Evaluation workflow

- Separate hyperparameter tuning from model evaluation through nested
  cross-validation.
- Evaluate tunable classifiers inside each outer split.
- Preserve raw outer-fold evaluation evidence.
- Select the best active classifier using mean outer F1-macro.
- Fit the selected classifier on the full dataset only after evaluation.
- Align stacking export CV with the training contract.
- Graduate stacking to a stable opt-in classifier.
- Remove post-selection CV from export.
- Avoid unnecessary SVC probability fitting during evaluation.
- Avoid nested estimator parallelism.

## Evaluation evidence and outputs

- Persist aggregate classifier evaluation results.
- Persist raw outer-fold evaluation evidence.
- Replace legacy CV-distribution plots with an F1-macro evidence figure.
- Plot raw outer-fold scores together with mean ± population SD and the
  selected classifier.
- Persist evaluation evidence figures as workflow artifacts.
- Propagate persistence failures instead of silently printing and ignoring
  them.

## Terminology and public contract

- Standardize the public terminology around **classifier**, **model**, and
  dataset **family**.
- Rename `[models]` configuration to `[classifiers]`.
- Rename CSV classifier identity from `model_name` to `classifier_name`.
- Stabilize the public Python API around:
  - `Config`
  - `load_datasets`
  - `plot_f1_macro_evidence`
  - `predict`
  - `__version__`
- Keep complete evaluation as a CLI workflow through `melite run`.

## Quick Start and distribution

- Add the packaged `melite example` workflow.
- Bundle a deterministic synthetic numeric tabular dataset with the package.
- Verify the installed example through wheel smoke testing.
- Make the README Quick Start work directly after installation without
  cloning the repository.
- Remove the redundant repository-level `examples/` workflow.
- Remove the redundant `environment.yml`; `pyproject.toml` is now the
  dependency source of truth.
- Add README contract tests to protect CLI commands, configuration
  terminology, local links, and version synchronization.

## Documentation

- Consolidate project documentation around Home, Usage, API Reference, and
  Changelog.
- Update the public project identity and evaluation terminology.
- Add the evaluation workflow figure and project visual assets.
- Align README and documentation with the v0.2.4 public API and packaged
  Quick Start.

## Engineering quality

- Add Ruff linting as a CI gate.
- Adopt Ruff formatting and enforce `ruff format --check`.
- Add Mypy type checking as a CI gate.
- Resolve the existing selected lint and local typing findings.
- Keep Python 3.11 as the minimum supported language target.

## Validation

- 182 tests pass locally.
- Ruff lint passes.
- Ruff formatting check passes.
- Mypy reports no issues in MELITE source modules.
- MkDocs strict build passes.
- Wheel/sdist smoke validation passes in CI.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- CI #64 is green.

## Compatibility notes

v0.2.4 includes intentional pre-stable schema changes:

- `[models]` → `[classifiers]`
- `model_name` → `classifier_name` in evaluation/result CSV surfaces

Legacy configuration/schema use is rejected explicitly rather than silently
interpreted.

title: Dev/v0.2.3. Add experimental stacking classifier workflow
body:
## Summary

This PR adds the MELITE v0.2.3 **experimental stacking** workflow.

Main changes:

- Adds an opt-in `stack` model key based on sklearn `StackingClassifier`.
- Keeps F1 macro as the main scoring and model-selection metric.
- Keeps standalone SVC behavior unchanged as `StandardScaler -> SVC`.
- Uses `stack_method="predict_proba"` for stacking.
- Uses a stacked SVC base estimator with `StandardScaler -> SVC(probability=True)`.
- Keeps Random Forest and XGBoost unscaled because they are tree-based models.
- Uses `LogisticRegression` as the initial final estimator.
- Preserves `.pkl` export through `joblib`.
- Adds export and prediction support for stacking models.
- Documents the stacking workflow and its internal CV behavior.
- Adds `.tmp_stack_smoke/` to `.gitignore` for local smoke-test outputs.

## Notes

The stacking-internal CV uses the configured split count and random state without repeated splits because sklearn stacking builds out-of-fold meta-features with `cross_val_predict`. This ensures each training sample contributes exactly one out-of-fold prediction for training the final estimator.

The outer MELITE grid search and reporting workflow still uses the existing repeated CV/F1 evaluation.

Optuna, MLflow, model registry behavior, and `.pkl` replacement are intentionally out of scope.

## Validation

Unit and integration validation:

- `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests\test_model_training.py tests\test_export.py tests\test_predict.py tests\test_version.py`
  - `47 passed`

  - `125 passed, 1 warning`

  - `MELITE 0.2.3`
- `python -m melite.cli --version`
  - `MELITE 0.2.3`
- `python -c "import melite; print(melite.__version__)"`
  - `0.2.3`

Real stack smoke test:

- Temporary TOML copied from `examples/example_config.toml`.
- Changed `[models].active` to `["stack"]`.
- Changed output path to `.tmp_stack_smoke/output/`.
- Ran `python -m melite.cli run --smoke --config .tmp_stack_smoke\stack_smoke.toml`.

  `python -m melite.cli export --config .tmp_stack_smoke\stack_smoke.toml --csv .tmp_stack_smoke\output\results.csv --outdir .tmp_stack_smoke\output --row 0 --force`

- Exported model:

  `.tmp_stack_smoke/output/Model_StackingClassifier_sample_pca70.pkl`

title: MELITE v0.2.2. Scale SVC with sklearn Pipeline and refine search grid
body:
## Summary

This PR prepares MELITE v0.2.2 with an SVC-specific preprocessing update and a focused SVC search-grid refinement.

SVC is now trained and exported as a scikit-learn pipeline:

```text
StandardScaler -> SVC
```

Scaling is applied only to SVC. RandomForestClassifier and XGBClassifier remain unscaled.

### Changes

- Wrapped SVC training in an sklearn `Pipeline` using `StandardScaler` followed by `SVC`.
- Updated SVC hyperparameter grids to use pipeline-compatible parameter names such as `svc__C`, `svc__kernel`, `svc__gamma`, `svc__degree`, and `svc__coef0`.
- Updated SVC export so exported SVC models preserve the same `StandardScaler -> SVC` pipeline used during benchmarking.
- Preserved legacy export compatibility for older SVC parameter dictionaries using unprefixed keys such as `C` and `kernel`.
- Kept RandomForestClassifier and XGBClassifier unscaled.
- Added a linear SVC block to the full SVC search grid.
- Adjusted polynomial SVC `coef0` grid from `0.02` to `0.2`.
- Updated tests covering config, model training, export, and prediction behavior.
- Updated version, changelog, README, citation metadata, and docs references for v0.2.2.

### Validation

- `python -m pytest tests -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp <temp-dir-outside-repo> -q`
-- 118 passed, 1 warning
- `python -c "import melite; print(melite.__version__, melite.__all__)"`
-- 0.2.2 ['Config', 'load_datasets', 'plot_cv_distributions', 'predict', '__version__']
- `git diff --check`
-- Passed


### Notes

- Public API unchanged.
- CLI behavior unchanged.
- Result schema unchanged.
- Prediction remains compatible with exported sklearn pipelines.
- RF and XGB grids were not changed.

title: MELITE v0.2.1. Hardening strict tabular workflows for v0.2.1
body:
## Summary

This PR prepares MELITE v0.2.1 as a focused hardening release for the strict tabular dataset architecture introduced in v0.2.0.

It does not add a major new feature. Instead, it strengthens model selection, export consistency, installed-package validation, and documentation/metadata.

## Changes

### Model training

- Fixed `[models].active` / `ACTIVE_MODELS` so it now controls which model families are trained.
- `MultiModelTrainer` now validates active model keys before training.
- Empty active model lists now fail clearly.
- Unknown model keys now raise a clear `ValueError`.
- Added tests confirming that single-model configurations such as `["svc"]` and `["rf"]` train only the requested model.

### Export hardening

- Hardened `export_best_model` to use strict dataset loading for registry-based datasets.
- Removed the unsafe legacy fallback to `arr.files[0]`.
- Individual legacy `.npz` files now require an explicit `X` array.
- Legacy reduction/level export compatibility remains supported.
- Aggregated legacy archives remain supported, with validation for:
  - 2D feature matrices
  - numeric feature matrices
  - matching `X`/`y` lengths

### Installed-wheel smoke workflow

- Added an installed-wheel smoke workflow using a minimal strict `[datasets.toy]` dataset.
- The smoke workflow:
  - builds the wheel,
  - installs it into a temporary environment outside the checkout,
  - verifies public API boundaries,
  - verifies the installed package is imported from the temporary environment,
  - runs `melite run --config toy_config.toml --smoke`,
  - runs `melite export --config toy_config.toml --row 0 --force`,
  - verifies expected output artifacts.
- Updated CI to run the new smoke workflow.

### Documentation and metadata

- Updated project metadata to v0.2.1.
- Updated `CHANGELOG.md` with the v0.2.1 hardening entry.
- Updated README and documentation to reflect:
  - strict `.npz` dataset expectations,
  - `[models].active` behavior,
  - export hardening,
  - installed-wheel smoke validation.
- Public API remains unchanged:

```python
["Config", "load_datasets", "plot_cv_distributions", "predict", "__version__"]
```

### Validation

The following validations passed locally:

```python
python -m pytest
python -m build --no-isolation
python scripts\smoke_install_wheel.py
python -c "import melite; print(melite.__version__, melite.__all__)"
git diff --check
```

Build output confirmed:

```bash
Successfully built melite-0.2.1.tar.gz and melite-0.2.1-py3-none-any.whl
```

The installed-wheel smoke workflow completed successfully.

### Notes

- This PR intentionally keeps legacy reduction/level export compatibility.
- Legacy individual .npz files must now contain an explicit X key.
- No public API expansion is introduced in this release.
- No PyPI publishing, tagging, or release creation is included in this PR.

title: MOSAIC v0.1.2 — Hardening Release
body:
## What's changed

This release focuses entirely on hardening and consolidation. No new features
or classifiers are introduced.

### Refactor
- Moved all source modules into a `mosaic/` Python package directory.
- Updated all intra-package imports to use the `mosaic.*` namespace.
- `result_manager.py` now reads `__version__` from `mosaic.version` instead of
  a hardcoded string.

### Added
- `--smoke` flag for lightweight benchmarking with single-value hyperparameter
  grids and 3-fold CV (no repeats). Useful for development and CI validation.
- `argparse` CLI in `mosaic.main` with `--help` support.

### Fixed
- Bumped version string to `0.1.2` in `version.py` and `CITATION.cff`.
- Added SPDX license headers to `model_training.py` and `plot_metrics.py`.

### Docs
- Updated `README.md` to reflect the `mosaic/` package structure, corrected
  CLI commands, and documented `--smoke` mode.
- Added v0.1.2 entry to `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Validation

All smoke tests passed in `mosaic_env` and scores match the v0.1.1 baseline:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| SVC PCA70 3-fold | f1: [0.7689, 0.9014, 0.8162] ✓ |
| XGBoost PCA70 3-fold | f1: [0.7319, 0.7848, 0.7166] ✓ |
| Random Forest PCA70 3-fold | f1: [0.7674, 0.9172, 0.7964] ✓ |
| PNG figure generation | ✓ |
| `--smoke` full PCA + UMAP run | ✓ |

## Notes

This is a **pre-release**. Not yet packaged for PyPI.

title: MOSAIC dev 0.1.1 hardening and metadata update
body:
## Summary

This PR prepares MOSAIC `dev/0.1.1` as a pre-stable hardening and metadata update before future packaging work.

## Changes

- Changed project license from MIT to GNU LGPL v3.0 or later.
- Added GNU license files:
  - `COPYING`
  - `COPYING.LESSER`
- Added citation metadata with `CITATION.cff`.
- Added centralized project version metadata in `version.py`.
- Added `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Rewrote `README.md` to reflect the current repository-based workflow.
- Added validation to ensure embedded `.npz` labels match `raw/labels.npy`.
- Ensured plot output directories are created automatically before saving figures.
- Added non-interactive model export support:

```bash
python export_best_model.py --row 0
```

## Validation

Validated locally in mosaic_env:

```bash
python -m py_compile config.py export_best_model.py load_dataset.py main.py model_training.py plot_metrics.py result_manager.py version.py
```

```bash
python -c "import version; print(version.__version__, version.PROJECT_LICENSE)"
```

Additional smoke validations performed during review:

- PCA70 dataset loading.
- SVC minimal training.
- Random Forest minimal training.
- XGBoost minimal training.
- PNG figure generation.
- .pkl model serialization.
- export_best_model.py --help.

## Notes

MOSAIC remains pre-stable and is not yet packaged for PyPI. This PR keeps the current script-based architecture while improving licensing, metadata, documentation, and basic runtime robustness.
